intent_snapshot.goal: Expose the Kernel's existing resolve_finding operation on the Claude Code Host MCP surface as defined by docs/specs/claude-host-resolve-finding.spec.md: one additive ordinary tool that carries task_id and finding_id into the existing ordinary-operation port, so a Claude Host imm-loop that has fixed and verified a finding's cause can clear it and let the Kernel reproject the next obligation, instead of terminating fail-closed on 'Kernel requires resolve_findings' with no reachable operation. This task_id succeeds the stopped 2026-09-06-001-claude-host-resolve-finding, whose round-1 QA findings could not be cleared on a Host that does not yet publish resolve_finding; the implementation and its evidence are unchanged and its terminal record is preserved under .imm/audit/2026-09-06-001-claude-host-resolve-finding/.

acceptance.assertion: listMcpTools() exposes a resolve_finding tool whose inputSchema declares both task_id and finding_id and requires exactly ["task_id", "finding_id"], and whose annotations are the ordinary non-privileged shape rather than privilegedAnnotations(), because canary_application.ts builds the Kernel action without a capability and the Pi Host imm-canary-work.ts already lists resolve_finding in its ordinary KERNEL_OPERATIONS. Calling the tool through createMcpRuntime on a fixture repository whose TaskRecord holds an open blocking finding resolves exactly that finding in the persisted TaskRecord, appends exactly one history entry, and moves the Kernel projection's next_obligation off resolve_findings; the assertion reads the resulting record and projection rather than only the tool listing, so a tool registered without working dispatch fails.

Every rejection path stays fail-closed with a byte-identical TaskRecord and zero Kernel writes: a missing or non-string finding_id is rejected by the adapter before any Kernel call, and an unknown finding id, an already-resolved finding, a non-active lifecycle, and the unresolved_user_decision and replan_required kinds each surface the reducer's KernelInvariantError unchanged, proving the adapter reads no findings, tests no kind, and adds no second authority. A connection with no bound host version and a connection that never negotiated interactive elicitation both reject the tool exactly as they reject advance_assurance. PRIVILEGED_OPERATIONS is unchanged, and the eight pre-existing tools keep their exact order, schemas, annotations, and dispatch. The checked-in plugins/immune-brain/dist/claude/mcp-server.mjs matches a fresh generate so the published surface cannot drift from its runtime source.

findings.summary: plugins/immune-brain/dist/claude/mcp-server.mjs was regenerated from a dirty worktree: it adds unrelated enrollCanaryTask batch-lineage code (input.batch, batch_head_lineage_broken, consumeChild/releaseChild) that has no source in this revision, since plugins/immune-brain/runtime/kernel/enrollment.ts is the identical blob 4fb5efe in base and review with zero batch references and runtime/kernel/batch_authority.ts is absent from tree 6ed3958, so checkClaudePlugin in the tests/claude-host-package.test.ts case 'checked-in mcp-server.mjs matches a fresh generate' fails on a clean checkout and the published server ships unreviewed enrollment behavior; regenerate the bundle from this revision's source only.

history.reason:
Review returned a valid blocking finding (the checked-in dist bundle carries batch-lineage code whose source is outside this task's scope and uncommitted, so a clean checkout of the review revision fails build-claude-plugin --check). Clearing it needs resolve_finding, which the loaded 3.6.4 plugin does not publish. The cause is fixed by committing the batch runtime work so the next enrollment's base_head contains it; the same scope re-enrolls on that base.
